relationConvention: family[otherId] is what that person is to me (e.g. 'child' = they are my child)
description: A river town of about 9,000 in the Upper Midwest, an hour north of Milwaukee. The economy is a cheese plant, a regional distribution warehouse, Millbrook Regional hospital, a community college, family farms and a struggling Main Street. A growing share of residents are immigrants or remote workers.

personas.name: Adaeze Okafor
personas.occupation: child-protective services caseworker for the county
quirks: keeps a paper planner color-coded by child
hums hymns while driving between home visits
personas.backstory: Adaeze came to the US at 24 for graduate school in Milwaukee and met Chidi at a Nigerian church picnic the following summer. For eleven years she has worked as a child-protective caseworker for the county, a job that sends her into the hardest kitchens in three townships and that she still believes in, most days. She carries 19 open cases and does her documentation at the dining table after Amara and Emeka are asleep. She is the household's planner: appointments, school forms and church rotas live in a paper planner she trusts more than any phone. Her mother calls from Enugu every Sunday asking when she will slow down.
personas.speechStyle: warm but precise; asks direct questions and waits for the answer
goals: get Amara into the regional gifted program
take the family to Nigeria for her mother's 75th birthday

personas.name: Chidi Okafor
personas.occupation: master electrician running a two-person contracting business
quirks: gives every client his cell number
watches Premier League replays at 6 a.m.
personas.backstory: Chidi trained as an engineer in Lagos, found the degree counted for little in Wisconsin, and rebuilt his career through a four-year electrical apprenticeship. Okafor Electric is now him, one apprentice and a white van, wiring new builds and fixing the farmhouses nobody else wants to touch. Work comes almost entirely by word of mouth, so he answers every call and remembers every customer's dog. Quotes and invoices happen late at night on his phone, and he loses at least one job a month to slow follow-up. He coaches Emeka's Saturday soccer team badly and enthusiastically.
personas.speechStyle: jovial storyteller; slips into Pidgin when excited

personas.name: Amara Okafor
quirks: corrects adults' grammar
reads under the covers with a headlamp
personas.backstory: Amara reads two grade levels ahead and is testing for the regional gifted program in the spring. She is fiercely protective of Emeka and fiercely annoyed by him. She wants to be a surgeon.
goals: get a card for the city library

personas.name: Emeka Okafor
quirks: narrates his own soccer games out loud
collects bottle caps
personas.backstory: Emeka is loud, sweet and almost never still; his teacher's notes home say 'delightful' and 'please work on sitting' in the same sentence. He plays on his father's soccer team, and his best friend is Eli Cohen from down the street.
personas.speechStyle: fast and excited, lots of 'and then'

personas.name: Erik Lindqvist
personas.education: high school; two years of agricultural college
quirks: checks the weather radio three times a day
fixes things with baling wire that should be thrown out
personas.backstory: Erik milked cows on the Lindqvist place north of town for 46 years, the third generation to do it, and sold the herd and most of the land in 2016 when milk prices and his knees gave out together. The sale left him and Marit comfortable on paper, but he still lives as if the next bad year is coming. He drives a 2004 pickup, pays cash, and distrusts anything that needs a password. Mornings are coffee at the Main Street diner with Walt Thompson and the same four men. He mentors Kenji Tanaka, who rents what is left of his land, more than Kenji asked for.
goals: keep the remaining 80 acres in the family

personas.name: Marit Lindqvist
quirks: writes thank-you notes on the same stationery since 1985
remembers every child in town by their reading level
personas.backstory: Marit ran the Millbrook Elementary library for 34 years and still volunteers there on Tuesdays. She keeps the extended family connected: birthday cards, Sunday dinners, and most of the after-school care for Nora and Leo since Karin's divorce. She uses a tablet her daughter set up, mostly for photos and video calls, and gets anxious when an app changes its layout. Since Erik's heart scare last year she quietly manages his medications and appointments.

personas.name: Karin Haas
personas.occupation: emergency department nurse at Millbrook Regional
quirks: eats lunch standing up even on days off
keeps a go-bag in the car
personas.backstory: Karin works three 12-hour night shifts a week in the emergency department and runs the rest of her life in the gaps. She and Ben divorced four years ago, amicably enough that they still split Leo's hockey driving, not amicably enough to sit together at games. Money is tighter than her salary suggests: she kept the house, and the mortgage plus two kids' activities eat most of it. She leans hard on her parents for childcare and feels guilty about it. Adaeze Okafor is the only person she lets see her tired.
personas.speechStyle: brisk, dark humor, no patience for vagueness

personas.name: Nora Haas
personas.occupation: high school junior; weekend job at the Reyes taquería
quirks: sketches on her forearm in ballpoint
plays the same playlist on repeat for weeks
personas.backstory: Nora works weekends at the Reyes family's taquería and is saving for a summer art program. She has been quieter since the divorce and is closest to her grandmother Marit. Her best friend is Ava Murphy.
goals: get into a summer art intensive

personas.name: Leo Haas
quirks: sleeps in his hockey socks before games
memorizes pro hockey stats
personas.backstory: Leo lives for hockey and the 5 a.m. ice times both his parents complain about. He is easygoing at home and loud at the rink, and he idolizes Liam Murphy, who is three years older and ignores him.
personas.speechStyle: short answers unless the topic is hockey

personas.name: Ben Haas
quirks: keeps a football schedule magnet on the van dashboard
always tips in cash
personas.backstory: Ben installs and repairs furnaces and air conditioners for a regional company, which means long winter days and on-call weekends. Since the divorce he rents a small house on Cedar Street and has the kids every other week. He is trying, unevenly, to be more present: he never misses a hockey game but forgets dentist appointments. He eats a lot of gas-station food and knows it. Friday nights are at the Rusty Anchor, where Jake Kowalski pours his beer.
goals: get more overnights with the kids

personas.name: Marisol Reyes
personas.occupation: owner of La Cocina de Graciela, a Main Street taquería
quirks: tastes every pot before service
keeps the books in a spiral notebook and a spreadsheet that disagree
personas.backstory: Marisol came to the US at 17 and spent a decade in other people's kitchens before opening the taquería seven years ago, named for her mother-in-law's recipes. It is the busiest lunch spot in town and barely profitable: costs keep climbing, and she won't raise prices on the plant workers who are her regulars. She works six days a week, and ordering, scheduling and payroll happen on her phone between rushes. She and Svetlana Ivanova, who used to do her taxes, are not on speaking terms after a dispute over fees.
personas.speechStyle: fast and warm; switches between Spanish and English mid-sentence

personas.name: Tomás Reyes
personas.occupation: line supervisor at the Millbrook Foods cheese plant
quirks: irons his work shirts on Sunday nights
keeps a running list of house repairs on the fridge
personas.backstory: Tomás has worked at the cheese plant for 15 years and supervises a 22-person shift, many of them recent immigrants who bring him their paperwork questions. He is steady where Marisol is fiery, and his union wage and health insurance are what make the restaurant possible. He plays Sunday rec-league soccer with Darnell Walker and some of the warehouse crew. His mother Graciela moved in two years ago after his father died, and he worries about her more than he says.
personas.speechStyle: calm, deliberate, polite to a fault
goals: help Sofia get into a good college

personas.name: Sofia Reyes
quirks: color-codes her notes
translates for her grandmother at appointments
personas.backstory: Sofia is a straight-A freshman who already talks about becoming a lawyer. She works the restaurant register after school and is her grandmother's translator and tech support. She looks out for Yui Tanaka in the robotics club.
goals: get a phone with a better camera

personas.name: Mateo Reyes
quirks: draws dinosaurs on every napkin at the restaurant
asks 'why' until adults give up
personas.backstory: Mateo is the restaurant's unofficial greeter and the regulars' favorite. He is in the same school as Amara Okafor, whom he finds intimidating.

personas.name: Graciela Reyes
personas.occupation: retired seamstress; cooks at the family taquería
quirks: lights a candle for her late husband every evening
refuses to measure ingredients
personas.backstory: Graciela sewed uniforms in a San Antonio factory for 30 years and moved to Millbrook into Tomás's spare room after her husband died. She speaks limited English and relies on Sofia for anything involving forms, phones or the pharmacy. Mornings she makes the tamales and salsas at the restaurant, the recipes it is named for. She is at Mass at St. Bridget's every Sunday and sits with Evelyn Brooks, though they share only a few words of a common language.

personas.name: Priya Patel
personas.occupation: senior product designer, remote, for a Chicago fintech company
quirks: redesigns restaurant menus in her head
has opinions about every app's onboarding
personas.backstory: Priya and Dana moved from Chicago two years ago for Dana's teaching job and more space to raise Iris, and Priya kept her remote design job. She works from a converted sunroom and the café on Main Street, often next to Josh Cohen. She tries new apps constantly, partly for work, and abandons most within a week. Small-town life is quieter than she expected: on bad days she feels isolated, and on good days she loves that the market vendors know Iris by name. Her flexible schedule has made her the default weekday parent, which is not the same as being free.

personas.name: Dana Chen
personas.occupation: biology instructor at Millbrook Community College
quirks: identifies birds by call mid-conversation
keeps a field notebook in every jacket
personas.backstory: Dana left a string of postdocs for a stable teaching job and doesn't regret it. She teaches four sections of biology, mostly nursing prerequisites full of students working night jobs, like Bianca Silva. She is the more cautious half of the couple, with money and with technology, and actually reads privacy policies. Weekends she takes Iris on long stroller walks along the river trail. She misses the mountains and is slowly learning to love flat land.
personas.speechStyle: thoughtful and precise; asks follow-up questions

personas.name: Iris Chen-Patel
personas.education: home daycare three mornings a week
quirks: waves at every truck
personas.backstory: Iris is 14 months old, newly walking, and attends a home daycare three mornings a week.

personas.name: Darnell Walker
personas.occupation: night shift lead at the regional distribution warehouse
quirks: listens to business audiobooks at 1.5x speed
meal-preps every Sunday
personas.backstory: Darnell moved from Milwaukee three years ago to be near his grandmother Evelyn after her fall, and stayed for the warehouse job, where he now leads the night shift. He drives Evelyn to church and her appointments and checks on her daily. He is ambitious and methodical, saving for a down payment and studying for a supply-chain certification online. He rents a duplex with Jake Kowalski, which works because they are barely home at the same time. As one of the few Black residents in town he notices things, and mostly keeps them to himself.
goals: buy a house within two years

personas.name: Jake Kowalski
personas.education: high school; one semester of college
quirks: remembers every regular's drink
has three unfinished projects in the garage
personas.backstory: Jake grew up in Millbrook, left for one semester of college and came back. He has tended bar at the Rusty Anchor for six years and hears everyone's business, which makes him the town's unofficial news service. Money arrives in cash tips and leaves just as fast; he has overdrafted more than once. He is trying to get on as Chidi Okafor's second apprentice and become the kind of person who wakes up at 6 a.m.
personas.speechStyle: loud, friendly, fluent in small talk

personas.name: Thanh Nguyen
quirks: explains every repair with a drawing on the invoice
refuses to fix cars he thinks aren't worth it
personas.backstory: Thanh arrived in Houston as a teenager in 1986, learned engines in a cousin's shop, and moved north 20 years ago to buy a garage nobody else wanted. Nguyen Auto is known for honest estimates; he will tell you not to fix a car. He keeps records in a carbon-copy invoice book and on a desktop computer from 2011. His public argument with Gary Stone over a transmission bill last year is still talked about. He is proud of Kevin and quietly disappointed that his son moved home.
personas.speechStyle: blunt and economical, with the occasional surprising joke
goals: see Kevin pass the CPA exam

personas.name: Linh Nguyen
quirks: tracks every coupon saving in a notebook
runs a cousin group chat spanning four states
personas.backstory: Linh met Thanh at a Vietnamese church in Houston and followed him north, reluctantly, for the garage. She has spent 18 years in the hospital billing office untangling insurance denials, and she is the family's financial planner. She budgets to the dollar and is the reason they own the house and shop outright. She does the shop's books on weekends. She worries that Kevin is drifting.
personas.speechStyle: polite and practical; asks about price first

personas.name: Kevin Nguyen
personas.occupation: part-time clerk at Bell's Hardware; studying for the CPA exam
quirks: has 40 browser tabs open at all times
tries every productivity app and none of them stick
personas.backstory: Kevin graduated in accounting from UW-Madison, lost his first job in a round of layoffs, and moved back into his childhood bedroom 'temporarily' 14 months ago. He works three days a week at Bell's Hardware, studies for the CPA exam at night, and has failed one section once. Friends ask him first about new apps and gadgets. He and Bianca Silva have been texting a lot.

personas.name: Evelyn Brooks
quirks: calls every young person 'baby'
keeps a handwritten pill schedule taped to the cabinet
personas.backstory: Evelyn nursed at a Milwaukee hospital for 40 years and moved to Millbrook a decade ago because her late husband wanted a quiet place to retire. After a fall three years ago her grandson Darnell moved to town to look after her, which she pretends to resent and treasures. She lives alone in a small house near St. Bridget's, uses a flip phone and a landline, and reads the newspaper front to back. She is sharp, opinionated, and the first to bring a casserole when someone is sick.

personas.name: Sean Murphy
quirks: recognizes most license plates in town
grills year-round, even in snow
personas.backstory: Sean has been on the eight-officer Millbrook police force for 26 years and a sergeant for ten. He knows nearly everyone, which makes the job both easier and harder. He is careful with money and skeptical of change, though he grudgingly runs the department's new records system. He coaches nothing but attends everything, and his friendship with Marek Novak is mostly about the high school football team.
goals: retire at 55 on a full pension

personas.name: Kelly Murphy
quirks: organizes the neighborhood holiday cookie swap
listens to true-crime podcasts while cleaning
personas.backstory: Kelly works four days a week at the town's only dental practice, alongside Ana Silva, whom she has taken under her wing. She is the social engine of the Murphy household: carpools, team-parent group chats, birthday parties. She researches big purchases obsessively and then buys whatever her friends recommend. With Ava starting college applications, she has become a spreadsheet person.

personas.name: Ava Murphy
quirks: keeps a countdown to graduation on her phone
makes short videos nobody in her family understands
personas.backstory: Ava is applying to colleges in Chicago and Minneapolis and badly wants to leave. She is student council president and lifeguards in the summer. She and Nora Haas have been best friends since kindergarten.

personas.name: Liam Murphy
quirks: eats five meals a day
wears shorts in January
personas.backstory: Liam plays on Marek Novak's varsity football team and is more talented than disciplined. He games late into the night, and his grades show it.
personas.speechStyle: monosyllabic with adults, loud with friends

personas.name: Omar Haddad
quirks: still makes house calls for a few elderly patients
quotes Arabic poetry when tired
personas.backstory: Omar has been one of Millbrook's three family doctors for 27 years; he trained in Beirut and Detroit, and his patients include Erik Lindqvist, Evelyn Brooks and half the cheese plant. He is overextended and talks about retirement without planning it. He is wary of new tools at work since the hospital's last software rollout doubled his charting time. He is wealthy by town standards and lives modestly.
goals: find a successor for his practice

personas.name: Rania Haddad
personas.occupation: coordinator of the library's English and citizenship program
quirks: always has a dish of ma'amoul out for guests
keeps a list of every student who passed the citizenship exam
personas.backstory: Rania raised Leila, then built the library's English and citizenship program from a folding table into three classes a week, many of the students from the cheese plant. Half of Millbrook's immigrant families know her by name. She is close with Adaeze Okafor and Marit Lindqvist, and she hosts the best dinners in town. She is excited by technology that helps her students and frustrated by anything that assumes everyone owns a laptop.
goals: win grant funding for an evening class

personas.name: Leila Haddad
personas.occupation: marketing manager at Millbrook Community Credit Union
quirks: drafts important texts twice
runs at 5 a.m. on the river trail
personas.backstory: Leila worked at a Minneapolis agency, burned out, and came home to run marketing for the credit union, a job that is half strategy and half sponsoring 4-H fairs. Last year she married Marek, whom she had known since high school. Her parents ask about grandchildren at every dinner, and she is not ready. Friends ask her whether an ad or a product is a scam.
goals: grow the credit union's under-35 membership

personas.name: Marek Novak
personas.occupation: history teacher and head football coach at Millbrook High
quirks: turns every conversation into a history lesson
keeps a whistle in his car's cupholder
personas.backstory: Marek grew up on a farm outside town, played football for Millbrook High, and came back to teach there. Coaching takes his evenings from August to November, and he spends his own money on kids' cleats more often than Leila knows. He is warm, a little old-fashioned, and trusted by parents across town. His friendship with Sean Murphy is the town's most reliable football conversation.
goals: buy a house with some land

personas.name: Ana Silva
quirks: keeps a running total of the grocery cart in her head
sings to Gabriel in Portuguese
personas.backstory: Ana's parents brought her from Brazil to Newark as a baby. She came to Millbrook at 22 following a boyfriend who later left, and stayed for the dental job and the schools. She raises Gabriel mostly alone, with her sister Bianca living with them and splitting rent. Every dollar is assigned: she budgets weekly, compares prices across two stores, and has no cushion for a car repair. Kelly Murphy at work has become a big-sister figure.

personas.name: Gabriel Silva
quirks: names every truck he sees
personas.backstory: Gabriel started kindergarten this fall and is obsessed with garbage trucks. His aunt Bianca is his favorite person after his mother. He plays with Maya Cohen at the park.

personas.name: Bianca Silva
personas.occupation: café barista; nursing-prerequisite student at the community college
quirks: has a different hair color every month
hears about new apps before her friends do
personas.backstory: Bianca followed her sister to Millbrook two years ago. She works mornings at the Main Street café and takes nursing prerequisites at night, including Dana Chen's biology class. She is the household's early adopter: she signs everyone up for free trials and forgets to cancel them. She babysits Gabriel when Ana works late. She and Kevin Nguyen have been texting a lot.

personas.name: Kenji Tanaka
quirks: checks commodity prices before he gets out of bed
names his tractors
personas.backstory: Kenji's grandfather started the Tanaka farm after the war, and Kenji now runs 900 acres, some of it rented from Erik Lindqvist. He was the first farmer in the county with GPS-guided planting and soil sensors, and he is genuinely excited about farm technology, though the margins rarely justify the purchases. Income swings with weather and prices; the family is land-rich and cash-poor. He works dawn to dark from April to November and sleeps through most of January.
personas.speechStyle: quiet and technical; enthusiastic once you get him going
goals: get Yui interested in the farm

personas.name: Hannah Tanaka
quirks: owns a label maker and uses it
shows houses in muck boots
personas.backstory: Hannah grew up in Des Moines, married into farming, and handles the farm's books, loans and insurance with an accountant's precision. Three years ago she got her real-estate license for steadier income, and she now sells most of the houses in town that change hands. She knows who is moving, who is divorcing and who is in trouble, and is discreet about all of it. She works with Svetlana Ivanova at tax time.
goals: get the farm debt under control

personas.name: Yui Tanaka
quirks: builds things from farm scrap
speaks in full paragraphs or not at all
personas.backstory: Yui is the youngest member of the high school robotics club, where Sofia Reyes looks out for her. She has no interest in farming, which her father is pretending not to mind.
personas.speechStyle: precise and shy, suddenly animated about robots

personas.name: Patricia Bell
quirks: calls customers 'hon' regardless of age
keeps her father's 1962 cash register on the counter
personas.backstory: Pat took over her father's hardware store 30 years ago and has kept it alive against two big-box stores in the county seat by knowing her customers and stocking the odd part nobody else carries. Kevin Nguyen is her part-timer, and he keeps pushing an inventory system she resists using. She divorced young and has lived with Gary Stone for 12 years without seeing a reason to marry. She sits on the Main Street business association and is the town's informal mayor. She rents the apartment above the store to Zoe Martin.
goals: keep the store open five more years
find someone to sell it to

personas.name: Gary Stone
quirks: has AM talk radio on all day
holds grudges with precision
personas.backstory: Gary drove long-haul for 35 years and retired with bad knees, a small pension and strong opinions. He met Pat when he stopped in Millbrook for a part and kept coming back. He tinkers with an old truck in the garage and helps at the store when he feels like it. He is still feuding with Thanh Nguyen over a transmission repair he insists was overbilled. He distrusts subscriptions, banks and anything 'in the cloud'.

personas.name: Kwame Mensah
personas.occupation: IT systems administrator at Millbrook Regional
quirks: runs a home server in his closet
beta-tests software for fun
personas.backstory: Kwame grew up in Kumasi, studied computer science in Columbus, Ohio, and took the hospital IT job five years ago for the cost of living. He is the person people call when something breaks, from the doctors' laptops to Kenji Tanaka's farm network. He lives alone, automates everything in his house, and tries most new technology the week it launches. He is quietly lonely and has been on more first dates in the county seat than he would admit.
personas.speechStyle: calm and nerdy; explains things patiently
goals: move into an IT director role

personas.name: Svetlana Ivanova
personas.occupation: runs a one-woman accounting and tax practice
quirks: works with two calculators
never rounds
personas.backstory: Svetlana emigrated in 1998, rebuilt her career from bookkeeping up, and runs a one-woman tax and accounting practice from a converted storefront, living upstairs. Her clients include the Tanakas, the Lindqvists and, until a fee dispute, Marisol Reyes. She was widowed six years ago and is raising Dmitri mostly alone. She is severe on first meeting and deeply loyal once she trusts you. She treats any tool that touches money with suspicion until she has tested it herself.

personas.name: Dmitri Ivanov
personas.occupation: community college student; night shift at the distribution warehouse
quirks: produces beats on a laptop at 3 a.m.
drinks energy drinks like water
personas.backstory: Dmitri takes two classes a semester at the community college and works nights at the warehouse on Darnell Walker's shift. He has no idea what he wants to do, which his mother finds intolerable and he finds normal. He makes electronic music and has a small online following.
personas.speechStyle: mumbled and ironic; opens up about music

personas.name: Rachel Cohen
personas.occupation: pharmacist at the Main Street pharmacy
quirks: reads the label on everything
runs the household from a kitchen whiteboard
personas.backstory: Rachel runs the pharmacy counter on Main Street and fills most of the town's prescriptions, which makes her a quiet authority on who is sick. She and Josh moved from Minneapolis four years ago for a bigger house and a slower life, and got half of that. She is the household's organizer and the one who notices the subscription charges on the card statement. Her days run back to back from school drop-off to closing, then a relay of homework, swim lessons and bedtime.
personas.speechStyle: efficient; warm with customers, clipped when stressed
goals: cut back to four days a week

personas.name: Josh Cohen
personas.occupation: senior software engineer, remote, for a Minneapolis health-tech company
quirks: has a standing desk and never stands
builds side projects nobody asked for
personas.backstory: Josh writes backend code from the basement and the Main Street café, where he and Priya Patel trade opinions about software. He handles school pickup and most weeknight logistics. He tries new tools quickly and pays for anything that saves time, which Rachel tolerates. He is restless in Millbrook and has quietly looked at jobs back in Minneapolis.
personas.speechStyle: casual and nerdy, prone to tangents
goals: get Rachel to take a real vacation

personas.name: Eli Cohen
quirks: builds elaborate brick cities
asks how everything works
personas.backstory: Eli is an inventive third grader whose best friend is Emeka Okafor. He wants to be an engineer like his dad, though he isn't sure what his dad does.

personas.name: Maya Cohen
quirks: performs dances at dinner
personas.backstory: Maya is a theatrical first grader who takes dance on Saturdays and narrates her day in great detail. She plays with Gabriel Silva at the park.

personas.name: Ruth Thompson
quirks: balances her checkbook to the penny every Sunday
bakes for every funeral
personas.backstory: Ruth worked at Millbrook State Bank for 38 years, back when it was locally owned. She and Walt have been married 52 years. She uses a smartphone her granddaughter Zoe set up, mostly for video calls and the church prayer list, and calls Zoe whenever an update moves a button. She sits with Evelyn Brooks at church and is the first to organize meals when someone is in the hospital.
personas.speechStyle: gentle, Midwestern nice, 'oh for Pete's sake'
goals: keep Walt out of the hospital

personas.name: Walt Thompson
quirks: raises the flag every morning
eats lunch at 11:30 sharp
personas.backstory: Walt sold tractors for 40 years and knows every farm in the county, which is why he and Erik Lindqvist hold court at the diner every morning. He served two years in the Army and is active at the VFW post. He has COPD from a lifetime of smoking he finally quit, and Ruth manages his medications. He has no interest in computers and is proud of it.
personas.speechStyle: folksy and slow; stories that get there eventually
goals: march in the Memorial Day parade

personas.name: Zoe Martin
personas.occupation: certified nursing assistant on the hospital's long-term care wing
quirks: has a playlist for every shift
color-codes her scrubs by weekday
personas.backstory: Zoe grew up in Millbrook, tried living in Madison for two years, and came back when her grandfather Walt's health worsened; her parents retired to Arizona. She works as a nursing assistant on the hospital's long-term care wing, where Karin Haas has become a mentor, and is saving for nursing school. She rents the apartment above Bell's Hardware from Pat Bell and is her grandparents' tech support. She and Bianca Silva became friends at the café.
